dedupe_keys.name: helics and saint co simulation framework for coupled natural gas and electricity networks benchmarked against the integrated saint model

description: This record describes a co-simulation framework for coupled natural gas and electricity networks, presented in a July 2022 Energies article indexed on OSTI. As reliance on gas-fired generation couples the two networks, constraints in one system affect the other, and the authors note that co-simulation results had rarely been compared with an integrated model. They build a co-simulation framework on the HELICS platform and the SAInt tool, which models transient gas flow and AC optimal power flow, and benchmark it against a fully integrated version of the SAInt power and gas simulators. Two test networks and a network representing the Belgian power and gas systems are tested under normal operation and with compressor disruptions, and the two approaches give nearly identical nodal pressure, gas flow rates and active power generation. Coverage is two test networks and one Belgian case. Access: the article record on OSTI, free; the framework code is not linked on the page read, and SAInt is a separate commercial tool. Caveats: three networks only. It suits gas-power interdependency and co-simulation research, and relates to the GRAZER coupled gas-power simulation record catalogued here.
